post.description: Takes a snapshot of the machine first and returns its id, so a failed resize can be undone. A bigger size grows the machine in place (it keeps its id, disk and running processes). A smaller size makes a new machine at that size and copies the home and work folders to it straight from the old machine, then moves this machine (same id, workspace bindings and grants) to it and deletes the old one: running processes are lost, the disk survives. A shrink answers `shrink.state: copying` until it is done; retry with the same clientKey to go on. Any failure deletes the new machine and keeps the old one unchanged. Retries with the same clientKey reach the same snapshot and the same resize.

get.description: The owner's env entries, decrypted while active, so a machine they added starts with their keys; a deleted entry reads as revoked with no value, so the machine removes it. Every entry carries its `delivery` and `allowedHosts`; an active proxy entry carries its value only for `delivery=proxy.v1` and otherwise reads `withheld`, so an older machine never puts it in an agent's environment. The bearer is a joined machine's credential (`cmm_`) whose owner granted it the vault (`vault: true` on the join token or PUT /v1/machines/{id}/vault), on the owner's personal team and minted by them; or the owner's own solo Cloud machine install token. A revoked machine answers 401; one never granted answers 403 vault.not_granted, and one whose grant lapsed 403 vault.grant_expired. The answer holds only the entries the machine's grant names.

schema.description: `proxy.v1`: this machine runs the egress proxy, so proxy entries carry their value. Without it a proxy entry reads `withheld` with no value.

400.description: vault.invalid_name: the name is not [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]* of at most 128, or is one the machine owns (PATH, HOME, LD_*, CMUX_*, ...). | vault.invalid_value: valueBase64 is not padded base64 of 1-16384 bytes. | vault.fingerprint_mismatch: fingerprint is not the lowercase sha256 hex of the value. | vault.invalid_hosts: allowedHosts is not 0-16 lowercase DNS names (optionally `*.` and `:port`). | vault.no_entry: the name has no active entry to set a policy on.

401.description: vault.unauthorized: a valid cmux access token or machine credential is required, or the machine was revoked.

403.description: vault.forbidden: this caller may not use this route (person routes refuse machines and agents). | vault.not_granted: the machine was never granted its owner's vault; the owner grants it with PUT /v1/machines/{id}/vault. | vault.grant_expired: the machine's grant lapsed; the owner renews it with PUT /v1/vault/grants/{kind}/{id}.

404.description: vault.not_found: the vault is not enabled on this deployment.

409.description: vault.limit: the user already has 100 env entries saved; delete one first.

503.description: vault.unconfigured: the deployment has no usable vault master key yet; retry later. | vault.unavailable: the store or a credential check is unreachable; retry.

tags.description: The team's agent mesh: every acpmux daemon heartbeats its sessions (POST /heartbeat), finds a session by name (GET /sessions), sends to it (POST /messages, a durable receipt at GET /messages/{messageId}), and long-polls its own inbox (GET /inbox), acking each message (POST /messages/{messageId}/ack). Delivery is at-least-once: a message stays leased to the receiving daemon until acked and expires after 7 days. The hub grants nothing; the receiving daemon applies its own rules.
tags.name: Mesh

tags.description: Development-only Auto placement. Pick (formerly place) is a dry run; create reserves team budget and creates idempotently by clientKey. Budget caps and usage come from the server's lease store, never the request. Queue and upgrade return no machine. A fallback is advisory and requires fresh admission; it never triggers a second create after an ambiguous error.
tags.name: Machine placement

tags.description: Development-only team machines. The offers endpoint merges normalized offers from every configured provider. Every other call is checked by the team machine policy (docs/team-machines.md): a team machine is listed, opened, resumed, paused and forked by any member; a private one only by its creator; deleting takes the creator or an admin; visibility is the creator's. A snapshot records who took it and inherits its machine's visibility at that moment; it is listed and forked under the same rules. A machine or snapshot the caller may not see answers 404. Every action but a read leaves an audit row, refusals included; members read the rows of what they can see and their own, admins all, billing the rows that change spend. Usage reports running hours by who started them, by creator and by machine; the team pays for all of them. A client attached to a machine posts its presence about every minute and deletes it on detach; every machine lists who is present. App-started chats on a machine (chat-access) are its creator's; the creator or an admin shares them with a member (chat-grants, PUT) and takes the share back in one call (DELETE). A grant never opens a private machine.
tags.name: Machines
